title: Imaging informatics, displays, and CAD
summary: Technologist-level PACS, RIS, EHR, and DICOM basics; which displays may be used to interpret mammograms and why display calibration matters; CAD and AI as decision support, not replacement; and data integrity, original-image retention, and patient identification in a digital workflow. Built from eCFR, the 2023 MQSA final rule, FDA guidance, NCI PDQ, NLM MeSH, and link-only DICOM.

visuals.title: Where do original digital mammograms live?
visuals.prompt: Select the system where a facility's original FFDM/DBT images are typically retained for MQSA recordkeeping.

hotspots.revealLabel: HIS/EHR: patient record and hospital information
PACS archive: originals typically retained here

feedback.a: The RIS manages radiology administration such as scheduling. It doesn't archive images.
feedback.b: The HIS/EHR holds the patient record and reports, not the original image files.
feedback.c: The unit acquires images, but long-term retention is in the archive.
feedback.d: Correct. FDA notes that original FFDM and DBT images are typically retained in the performing facility's PACS.
feedback.e: The display shows images. It isn't the retention store.

visuals.explanation: Originals stay in the performing facility's PACS, and copies are what usually get released to other sites.
visuals.accessibilityNote: Each box is announced by its system name. Feedback explains each system's role.

visuals.title: Which category never marks the image?
visuals.prompt: Select the category of software that notifies clinicians about time-sensitive studies but does not mark locations on the image or remove cases from the reading queue.

feedback.a: CADe's job is to mark or highlight regions that may be abnormal.
feedback.b: CADx characterizes lesions as suspicious. It provides information about specific lesions.
feedback.c: Correct. § 892.2080 says triage software doesn't mark the image or remove cases, and it runs alongside standard care.

visuals.explanation: CADt prioritizes and notifies. CADe marks. CADx characterizes. None replaces the clinician.
visuals.accessibilityNote: Boxes are announced by category name and regulation number. The function appears only after answering.

visuals.title: Which set meets MQSA retention?
visuals.prompt: An archive holds only one of these sets for each exam. Select the set FDA would generally consider the original mammograms for MQSA retention.

hotspots.revealLabel: Permanent CAD marks only: not sufficient

feedback.a: Correct. Lossless compression allows complete reconstruction, so the images are generally treated as originals.
feedback.b: Lossy compression discards data. Without the full files, the facility no longer holds originals.
feedback.c: CAD marks must be removable. A permanently marked set alone doesn't meet retention.

visuals.explanation: FDA Responses 98 and 100 (88 FR 15126): lossless is generally original, lossy is not, and CAD marks must be removable.
visuals.accessibilityNote: Sets are announced by letter, and each box's text describes its storage method.

visuals.title: Which plan creates exact copies?
visuals.prompt: Select the contingency plan element that requires procedures to create and maintain retrievable exact copies of electronic health information.

feedback.a: Correct. The data backup plan creates and maintains retrievable exact copies.
feedback.b: Disaster recovery restores lost data, usually from the backups.
feedback.c: Emergency mode keeps critical processes running securely during an emergency.

visuals.explanation: 45 CFR 164.308(a)(7)(ii) separates backup (copies), disaster recovery (restore), and emergency mode operation (continue securely).
visuals.accessibilityNote: Boxes are announced by plan name.

glossary.definition: Information system for radiology's administrative activities such as scheduling and tracking exams.
Hospital-wide integrated system for administrative and clinical information.
Electronic record that carries a patient's health information across providers and locations.
Picture archiving and communication system: image storage, communication, and review. Original digital mammograms are typically retained here.
Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine: the predominant standard for imaging communication and storage. MQSA does not mandate it.
A vendor's published description of which DICOM services and objects a product supports.
DICOM's perception-based calibration curve that keeps grayscale images consistent across displays and printers.
Compression that allows complete reconstruction. Losslessly compressed mammograms are generally originals under MQSA.
Compression that discards data. Lossy images generally are not original mammograms under MQSA.
Computer-aided detection: marks or highlights possible abnormalities for the clinician. Not a replacement for the radiologist's review.
Computer-aided diagnosis: characterizes lesions, for example as suspicious for cancer. The clinician makes the decisions.
Computer-aided triage and notification: alerts clinicians about time-sensitive studies without marking images or removing cases.
The property that data have not been altered or destroyed in an unauthorized manner.
